purpose: Bounded non-England anchor review. Test whether Norse Greenland can add a quantitative global scale constraint without confusing an observed hostile-island population with intrinsic local capacity.

disposition_summary.reason: The whole-colony demographic interval (~1,400-2,200 at the AD 1300 peak) is not a capacity interval. The archaeological settlement boundary is dispersed and not mapped to EU5, local-food share is unresolved, and literature contains materially higher population model envelopes.

quality_gate.reason: No candidate passed the same-boundary local-food capacity and EU5 crosswalk requirements. The evidence is retained as a held-out hostile-island diagnostic rather than weakened into a target.

next_research_queue: Digitize Eastern and Western Norse Settlement archaeological farm polygons and map them to EU5 location footprints.
Find a same-boundary food-energy or sustainable-population estimate that separates local pastoral/marine production from overseas trade.
Reconcile the 1,400-2,200, 2,000-3,000 and 4,000-6,000 population model envelopes before assigning any upper endpoint.
